2.2       The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of SSI should make SWOT- anlysis as the tool of  management for SSI Units  by
overcoming the weaknesses  and threats to the SSI sector and availing the opportunities and strength , thereby, making the SWOT –Analysis
as tool for Management by Objective and policy intervention.
 
3.0       Policy iniatitves taken by Government  during the financial year 2005-06
 
3.1       Though the State Governments are primarily responsible for the promotion and development of SSI, the Central Government took
several policy initiatives for small enterprises sector during 2005-06:
193 items reserved for exclusive manufacture in the SSI sector have been dereserved in FY 2004-05. The total number of reserved items now
stands at 506.
As announced in the Budget 2005-06, the turnover eligibility limit under the General SSI Excise Exemption Scheme has been raised from
Rs.3 crore to Rs.4 crore.
With a view to integrating small and medium enterprises, facilitating their growth and enhancing their competitiveness (including measures to
reduce the rigours of the  “Inspector Raj” faced by the sector), the ‘Small and Medium Enterprises Development (SMED) Bill, 2005’ has been
introduced in the Lok Sabha.
A ‘Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to Small and Medium Enterprises’ has been announced by the Government.
Under the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) for Technology Upgradation, amendments have been made with effect from 29
th
September 2005 which, inter alia, include raising ceiling on loans from Rs.40 lakh to Rs.1 crore and the rate of subsidy from 12 per cent to 15
per cent.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has formulated the scheme of Small Enterprises Financial Centres (SEFC) under which banks will be
encouraged to establish mechanisms for better co-ordination between their branches and branches of Small Industries Development Bank of
India (SIDBI) in the identified clusters for more efficient credit delivery.
To facilitate technology upgradation and enhancing competitiveness, the investment limit (in plant and machinery) has been raised from Rs.1
crore to Rs.5 crore in respect of 69 additional items reserved for manufacture in the small scale sector and for all items in the drugs and
pharmaceuticals sector.
A new “Package for Promotion of Micro and Small Enterprises” is being formulated. This would include supplementary measures to
encourage adequate credit flow, further incentives for technology upgradation, infrastructural and marketing facilities, capacity building of
micro and small enterprises, support to women entrepreneurs, etc.
 
3.2       The small scale industries (SSI) constitutes one of the vibrant sectors of the Indian economy in terms of employment generation, the
strong entrepreneurial base it helps to create and its share in industrial production and exports.  During 2004-05, the small enterprises sector
registered a growth rate of 10 per cent as against a growth rate of 8.4 per cent for the overall industrial sector. During 2003-04, the
contribution of Small Enterprises Sector in the Gross Domestic Products (GDP) was 6.71 per cent.
 
3.3       The Committee understands that along with agriculture and organized large industries, the small enterprises sector including both SSI
and services provide the largest employment generation potential in the country.  The committee is of the view that Government should make
comparative assessment of Small Scale Industries vis-à-vis other Industries on the basis of growth rate, and chalk out strategy for   enhancing
further the employment generation potential, maxmising contribution to national exechequer, in order to  combat the problem of poverty and
improving  the standard of living and thus making real contribution to the National Economy.
 
3.4 The Committee is of the view that for streamlining and strengthening the contribution of small enterprises sector in the national economy,

Providing full credit, technology upgradation, modernization and marketing support to the SSI sector;
Infrastructure upgradation in general and particularly in the major small enterprises clusters; these would include road connectivity, regular
supply of power, common effluent treatment facility and water supply, etc.

4.0 Charter of functions of  Ministry of Small Scale Industries
 
4.1 The Government created the Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Agro and Rural Industries (SSI&ARI) in October, 1999 as the   nodal
Ministry for formulation of policy and co-ordination of Central assistance relating to promotion and development  of the small scale industries
in India. The Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Agro and Rural Industries (SSI&ARI) was bifurcated into two separate Ministries,
namely, Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries in   September, 2001. Taking into account the high
potential for growth in the SSI sector in terms of output, employment and exports, the role of the Ministry of Small Scale Industries is to
strengthen the SSI sector, to enable it to remain competitive in market-led economy and generate additional employment opportunities. For
achieving these objectives, the endeavor of the Ministry is to provide the SSI sector proper and timely inputs like adequate credit from
financial institutions/banks; funds for technology upgradation and modernization; adequate infrastructural facilities; modern testing facilities
and quality certification laboratories; modern management practices and skill upgradation through advanced training facilities;  marketing
assistance; and level playing field at par with the large industries sector.
 
4.2 The Committee understands that the Ministry of SSI designs policies, programmes, projects and schemes in consultation with its
organizations and various stakeholders and monitor their implementation with a view to assisting   the promotion and growth of small scale
industries. The committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should not only  advocate the  policy on behalf of the SSI sector with
other Ministries/Departments of the Central Government and the State and Union Territories for the promotion and proliferation of SMEs but
also co-opreate and  co-ordinate with them in the implementation of schemes projects prepared in this regard.
5.0 Organizational structure of Ministry of SSI
 
5.1 The Ministry of Small Scale Industries designs and implements the policies through its field organizations for the promotion and growth
of small scale industries.  The implementation of policies and various programmes/schemes for providing infrastructural and support services
to small enterprises is undertaken through its attached offices, namely Small Industries Development Organisation (SIDO), its field offices,
and National Small Industries Corporation Limited (NSIC), a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of SSI. Secretary (SSI) reviews
and monitors the functioning of organisations under the Ministry, implementation of plan schemes and various developmental activities on
fortnightly basis. The present monitoring mechanism has been found to be effective.
 
5.2 The Committee is of the view that monitoring mechanism of the Ministry of SSI should aim at developmental supervision which would
lead to carrying out the schemes and programmes efficiently and effectively in time and without cost over-run. 
 
6.0       Proposal of re-christening of the Ministry of SSI into the Ministry of Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) 
 
6.1       The Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Agro and Rural Industries (SSI & ARI) was carved out of the erstwhile Department of
Industrial Development (DID) on 14
th October, 1999 with a view to providing focused attention for promotion and development of small
scale industries.   The Ministry of SSI & ARI, thereafter on 1st September, 2001 was bifurcated into the Ministry of Small Scale Industries
(SSIs) and the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries. As per the Allocation of Business Rules notified on 6th September, 2001 the Ministry of
SSI, now, has the entries which include  coordination of the Development of Small Scale Industries, other than cottage and Village Industries
and Tiny/Micro Enterprises and Small Industries Board and National Small Industries Corporation Limited.
      
6.2       The Ministry is the nodal Ministry for policy formulation, promotion, development and protection of Small Scale Industries (SSIs). At
present all industries with an investment upto Rs. 1 (one) crore in Plant and Machinery whether held on ownership term or on lease or by hire
purchase come under the purview of this Ministry.  This limit in respect of 41 items covering hosiery, Pharmaceuticals, Stationery and hand
tools has been enhanced to Rs. 5.00 crore.   Further in 1991 Government also decided to extend the benefit being enjoyed by the SSIs to some
of the industry related service & business enterprises with investment in fixed assets, (excluding land & building) upto Rs. 10.00 lakhs
irrespective of the location of the units. 
                       
6. 3      The Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC) had recommended that:
 
                         “The inclusion of services and the enlargement of the scope of the Ministry to medium establishment are important in the
context of the emergence of sunrise knowledge-based industries as the harbinger of a new industrial revolution. New knowledge based
industries like pharmaceuticals and biotechnology industries to be internationally competitive and will require encouragement and support in
the initial period of their development. The emergence of IT and of software in a large way in this country also suggests the need for bringing
the service sector prominently into the ambit of encouragement and support given to small and medium establishments.  The scope of 
Ministry of SSI  should be enlarged to cover the service sector in addition to the manufacturing sector and to define and include medium

6 4       The ERC was of the view that to provide an environment for the natural growth of small establishments, the industrial establishments
(including the service sector) be divided into the following four categories on the basis of investment limits.
i.          Tiny                              Upto Rs. 25.00 lakh
ii.        Small     Above Rs. 25.00 lakh & upto Rs. 5.00     crore
iii.         Medium; and                Above Rs. 5.00 crore & upto Rs. 10.00 crore

6.5       The ERC has further suggested that industrial units should have the opportunity and be encouraged to transit from tiny to small to
medium and big establishments without any policy induced discouragement. 
 
6.6       The Committee is of the considered view  that  keeping in view  the overall global scenario, it is most appropriate and desirable to
adopt the nomenclature suggested by the ERC and accordingly change the nomenclature of the Ministry of SSI to that of the Ministry of
Small & Medium Enterprises and that also   to implement the objectives, achievements  and targets of Indian SMEs as set by Finance Minister
in General Budget 2006-07 and the years to come .
 
7.0 Action Plans set for the Ministry for the year 2006-07
 
7.1 The Action Plan for the Ministry for the year 2006-07 is stated  as under:-
 
Formulation of a single legislation to promote the growth of the sector and free it from  ‘Inspector Raj’;
Formulation of a Package for Promotional of Micro and Small Enterprises;
Examination of problems facing Enterprises in the Unorganised / Informal Sector through the National Commission set up for this purpose;
Facilitate credit flow to the SSI Sector – by effective implementation of ‘Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to SMEs’;
Infrastructure upgradation in major industrial clusters; and
Institutional reforms in terms of: (i) Decentralisation; (ii) Simplification; (iii) Transparency; (iv) Accountability; and (v) E-governance.
 
7.2 The Committee recognizes that the  organizational structure of Ministry of SSI have proved effective as an instrument of implementation
of various  policies, programmes/schemes relating  to Ministry of Small Scale Industries during 2005-06. The Committee is pleased to note
that  the present organisational set up has been quite effective and efficient however, the Ministry of SSI, keeping in view  the emergence of
SMEs, which has been well recognized in its Action Plan,    would need some re-orientation of form and retraining of staff to enable it to
make full use of the opportunities and challenges in the future. The Committee, accordingly , recommends that following iniatives may be
undertaken :-
More regular appraisal of policy initiative for the SME sector in similar countries;
Ascertaining best practices within the Central Government and also abroad for promotion and development of SME sector and their
adoption/adaptation in the Indian SME context;
Closer and more structural interaction with the stakeholders;
Improving synergies among the constituent organizations of the Ministry and the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries;
Promoting constructive competitiveness among field level organizations based on well defined objectives and action plans;
Retraining of staff, as appropriate.
 
7.3 The Committee hopes that once the requisite  steps are taken and adequate   precautionary measure are undertaken to achieve the Action
Plan subsequent to the  constant review and monitoring of the Action Plan, there should not be any problem in achieving the targets set in the
Action Plan 2006-07.

8.1.1 The Committee is constrained to express its displeasure  over the reduced budgetary allocation to the Ministry of SSI during the year
2006-07. Against the  projected  sum of Rs. 574.68 crore  (inclusive of Rs. 3.60 crore for works Outlay provided in the Demands of Ministry
of Urban Development) for the year 2006-07, the  Planning Commission has fixed the Annual Plan Outlay at Rs. 469.93 crores (inclusive of
Rs. 3.60 crore for works Outlay provided in the Demands of Ministry of Urban Development). The Committee wonders as how the Ministry
of SSI would manage the budgetary gap while achieving the originally envisaged objectives and action plan.
 
8.1.2    The Committee is anguished to observe that the budgetary allocation has been reduced under the Ministry’s demands for   Credit
Guarantee Fund Scheme where the proposed demand was Rs. 206.00 crore but the Planning Commission has approved only to the tune of  
Rs. 118.10 crore.  Similarly, under the Head Science & Technology, Research and Development, the proposed demand was Rs.  21.85 crore
while the same was approved to the tune of Rs.  16.85 crore  only. 
 
8.1.3    The Committee understands that Credit Gurantee Scheme is significant so far the credit to the SSI sector is concerned. And the net
credit to the SSI sector by the Public Sector Bank as the percentage to the total credit is dwindwling to the level of 9.8%.  The Finance
Minister , on the one hand understands the need for gearing up the SSI sector, considering its  importance as the “Engine of Growth” and
having the employment –generation potential but on the other hand,  the Planning Commission has  reduced the budgetary allocation under
the Credit Gurantee Scheme against the  projected demand by the Ministry of SSI for the year 2006-07.  The Committee is unable to
understand  the basic logic behind such budgeting, where there remains enormous gap between the policy and finance required to  to support
the  programme/scheme under the policy.
 
8.1.4    The Committee is of the considered view that Science & Technology, Research and Development is very much beneficial for any
industrial activities so far as  the cost-reduction, product-development, product - design etc. is concerned, therefore, reducing the budgetary –
allocation against the projected demand by the Ministry of SSI would amount to cutting the R&D activities, thereby, the margin of the profits
.
 
8.1.5    The Committee, therefore, desires that the Planning Commission would pay due attention to the proposals of the Ministry of SSI at the
R.E. stage and accordingly allocate the demands as per the requirement of the SSI sector.

9.2  The Ministry of SSI apprised the Committee that there is no major policy shift for the year 2006-07 as compared to 2005-06. The
endeavor of the Ministry is to strengthen and facilitate the SSI sector to enable it to remain competitive in the global economy and generate
additional employment.
 
9.3       Replying to the Committee’ query as to what extent the provision made in the budget proposal of Ministry of Small Scale Industries
for the year 2006-07  is an instrument of directing the national economic policy and  whether there is any change in economic philosophy in
the budget proposal of Ministry of Small Scale Industries for the year 2006-07 as compared to 2005-06, the ministry of SSI has stated that the
national economic policy focuses on employment generation.  SSI sector is one of the largest employment providers. Emphasis has been laid
for extensive promotion of the SSI sector which is recognised as an ‘Engine of Growth’.  The Budget allocation for the sector has therefore
been raised to Rs. 466.33 crore (exclusive of Rs. 3.60 crore for Works Outlay provided in the Demands of Ministry of Urban Development) in
2006-07 as compared to Rs. 408.91 crore (exclusive of Rs. 3.35 crore for Works Outlay provided in the Demands of Ministry of Urban
Development) in 2005-06. The economic philosophy behind the budget proposal in 2006-07 largely remains the same as in 2005-06.
 
9.4       Enumerating the economic philosophy behind the budget proposals explaining to what extent, the provision, affecting Ministry of
Small Scale Industries conform to the logistic of on-going liberalization and globalization process, the ministry of SSI explained that to
address the issue of liberalization and gloablisation for the SSI sector, and to assist the SSI sector to function in a competitive environment,
emphasis has been given for the technology upgradation of the SSI units. An enhanced budget provision of Rs.55.10 crore has been provided
during 2006-07 under the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS).  A budget provision of Rs.18.00 crore has also been provided
during 2006-07 under the ISO 9000/14000 Reimbursement Scheme. Under the Scheme, a maximum grant of Rs.75,000 is provided to the SSI
unit for adopting ISO- 9000/14000 quality and environment standards to make it globally competitive.
 
9.5 Liberalization and globalization
 
9.5.1    To help the SSI sector face the challenges posed by liberalisation and globalisation, the Government has been taking several policy
initiatives. These include dereservation of items reserved exclusively for manufacture in the SSI sector in a phased manner, enhancing the
investment limit in plant and machinery from Rs.1 crore to Rs.5 crore in 140 select hi-tech and export oriented sectors, etc besides all items in
the drugs and pharmaceuticals. The Government has also introduced a Small and Medium Enterprises Development Bill 2005 in the Lok
Sabha on 12
th May 2005 to facilitate the promotion and development of these enterprises and enhance their competitiveness. 
 
9.5.2    The Committee is of the view that Government should make efforts for achieving the goals towards liberalization and globalization in
the SSIs sector of the economy particularly, in the areas where liberalizing reforms remain to be achieved and  chalk out the  strategy  for 
achieving  the same within stipulated timeframe.

Government on formulation of appropriate policies, schemes, projects and programmes and on the other, implements these policies, schemes,

16.2     Office of the DC(SSI) maintains liaison with the Central Ministries, Planning Commission, State Governments and financial

16.3     The monitoring mechanism of Office of the Development Commissioner (SSI) on policies and programmes for promotion and

Small Scale Industries Board is an apex advisory body, constituted to render advice to the Government on all issues pertaining to small scale

16.4     The Committee is in agreement with the views of the Ministry of SSI that the role of the Office of DC (SSI) should be  reoriented,
broadly on the following lines in the changing scenario of liberalization and globalization:-
 
(a) In view of the world-wide trend, now also recognized in India, it is necessary to treat the small and medium enterprises (SME) as a
composite sector so as to facilitate their promotion and development, enhance their competitiveness and encourage the graduation of tiny to
small and small to medium enterprises. Towards this, the Office of the DC (SSI) would need to equipped and strengthened to view the sector
as a composite whole, without losing the focus on the need for generation of employment as well as the specific developmental/promotional
requirements and inter-linkages of each distinct component of the composite sector and the products and services produced by them.
 
(b) To address the issues of liberalization and globalization, the Ofiice of DC (SSI) need to widen and continuously update its knowledge base
regarding global trends in policies and Government interventions as well as ascertain ‘best practices’ in this field, within the country and
abroad, and appropriately adopt them.
 
(c) It would need to strengthen its linkages with the State Governments, other Central Ministries/Departments and associations of SMEs to
achieve the objectives more effectively.
 
(d) Finally, it would need to forge stronger links with the relevant international institutions and bilateral organizations for more effective
cooperation so as to derive full advantage of the comparative strengths of the Indian SME sector.

Development Bill, once constituted would play  pro- active role in facilitating and co-ordinating the inter institutional linkages among the
Organisations of Central/State Governments for the groth and development of SEs and MEs in India.

 18.2    At present Small Scale Industries are governed by Industries (Development  & Regulation) Act 1951.However the Acts/rules and
regulations are formulated by various authorities at the Central Government State Government level and Local authorities. These legal
regulations can be classified into labour related issues,tax related issues finance related issues ,location related issues ,product related issues
,environment related issues and safety, security, hygiene, health and welfare related issues, etc.
 
18.3     The regulatory frame work, particularly pertaining to Labour related Laws is cumbersome and in this regard the plethora of laws, rules
and regulations that have accumulated over the last several years of control regimes have become truly oppressive. The burden of inspections
under various laws has proved to be too onerous to bear. They have adverse bearing on the promotion and development of Small Scale
Industries.
 
18.4     All the industries including Large, Medium and Small Scale mentioned in schedule I of the ID&R Act, fall under the purview of
Industrial Development and Regulation (IDR) Act 1951 .However, those units employing 50/100  or less workers , with /without power do
not fall under the purview of ID&R Act. As has been already explained in the first para , plethora of  laws rules and regulations and the
burden of inspections under these, have crippled the SSI Sector. Therefore with a view to simplify these laws, rules and regulations and
streamline the system of inspections, Small  and Medium Enterprises Development Bill,2005is proposed to be enacted. It contains,  inter-alia,
provisions to simplify existing Labour Laws and streamline inspections, to wipe out the tyranny of Inspector Raj.
 
 18.5    The Committee understands that legal framework affecting the Small Scale Industries is not conducive and satisfactory, therefore, the
Committee feels that  in order to give fillip to the promotion and development of Small Scale Industries, the following immediate measure
may be undertaken :- 
 
A single Unified Act governing the rules pertaining to retrenchment and layoffs and social benefits for employees.
 
Enactment of SMED Bill, 2005.
 
Comprehensive Social Security Scheme for widening the social safety nets.
 
Since the Inspector Raj is causing severe harassment to Small Scale Units, therefore, the provision made in the proposed legislation for giving
good bye to Inspector Raj to wipe out the tyranny  of Inspector Raj.
 
18.6     Since the issues relates to Ministry of Labour and Employment, therefore, the committee recommends that the Ministry of SSI should
coordinate with Ministry of Labour and Employment at the earliest and effectively, and furnish the Committee outcome of the efforts so
undertaken by the Ministry.
 
19.0     Formulation of National Policy for Small Scale Industries.
 
19.1     The Comprehensive Policy Package      aims to strengthen the SSI Sector to be able to meet the fast changing economic scenario and
be able to face the challenges of the domestic and global competition due to liberalization of economy and introduction of WTO regime.  The
main emphasis is on easy credit availability, technological, modernization, infrastructural development, marketing support, etc.  The existing
policies /schemes have been framed keeping in view the ground realities and are being reviewed from time to time with stake holders to
enforce the corrective/supportive measures  required to make them suitable, sufficient and  effective for supporting the promotion and
development of Small Scale Industries .
 
19.2     The emphasis in existing policies and schemes  has accordingly been laid on easier access to credit, availability of collateral free
composite loans up to Rs.25 lakhs to assist small/tiny units through Credit Guarantee Schemes, introduction of Laghu Udyami Card Scheme,
marketing support through the schemes like SSI-MDA Schemes, providing subsidy for technological upgradation through the Credit Linked
Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology Up gradation, encourage obtaining of ISO-9000/4001 Certification by providing 75% (not exceeding
Rs.75000/-) of the cost,  infrastructure development through IID scheme, since extended to all areas with 50% reservation each for tiny sector
and rural areas, increase in project limit under National Equity Fund to Rs.50 lakhs,  and cluster development schemes, etc.  The funds are
also provided to State Governments to develop and upgrade the Mini Tool Rooms and to industry associations for setting up of Testing
Centres and sub-contracting exchanges.
 
19.3     The Committee  feels that there is the need for Comprehensive  National Policy for strengthening the Small Scale Sector, although the
process has already started  since 1991 in the sporadic manner, the need is to consolidate and streamline the national policy.  Keeping in view
of the dynamic situation of the Indian SSI sector vis-à-vis domestic & international industrial & economic environment, the Committee feels
that  that SSI policy must have been  revisited and revisied incorporating components viz programmes for infrastructure development,
technological upgradation, marketing support, easier access to creditand scientific management for inter-sectoral cooperation for ensured
promotion and proliferation of SMEs.

20.1     The Office of DC (SSI) has started a large number of Cluster Development initiatives under a holistic approach with active
involvement of beneficiary units through their Associations in its implementation. The activities taken up for development of the clusters are
demand based. Cluster Development initiatives initiated by DC (SSI) have generally resulted into technology upgradation, design
development, upgradation of skills, increased production  & exports and overall increase in competitiveness of the clusters.
 
20.2     Accordingly the Ministry selected 60 clusters from all over the country including the backward areas and the North-Eastern region.
The list has been forwarded to RBI for dissemination of public sector banks for incorporating the credit requirements of clusters in the State
Credit Plans.  It has also been recommended that one Lead Bank be identified for each cluster for coordinating the Credit Plan.
20.3     The Ministry also sensitized the concerned State Secretaries/Directors of Industries by writing a letter to them to draw their attention
for implementing the decision of incorporating the credit requirements of SSI units in the identified clusters in the State Credit Plan.  At the
SLBC’s meetings, issues relating to credit to SSI sector are coordinated by the State Secretary/Director of Industries, the latter have been
requested to impress upon the Convenor of SLBC to make assessment of the needs of SSIs in the clusters in consultation with other banks,
formulate Annual Credit Plan for the identified clusters in their State and get it incorporated in the State Credit Plan.  The State Governments
have also been requested to develop a monitoring mechanism for effective implementation of cluster Credit Plan.
 
20.4     To enhance the Cluster Development Model to promote and proliferate SMEs  Government can besides implementing cluster
development initiatives play useful role in ensuring setting up of conducive policies and schemes that encourage local cluster level collective
action, provide funding assistance to encourage  commercial and private institutions to take up cluster development and assist building
suitable linkages of the clusters with public and private institutions in the areas of financing, investments, infrastructure development and
social development.  The Ministry of Small Scale Industries has recently circulated detailed guidelines for selection and implementation of
interventions to small industry clusters under the SICDP.
 
20.5     The Committee appreciates  the announcement  of the Finance Minister made in his Budget Speech (2006-07) that the Cluster
Development Model can be usefully adopted not only to promote Manufacturing but also to renew industrial towns and build new Industrial
Township. The Committee also makes note of the decision of  the Prime Minister to constitute an Empowered Group of Ministers to  lay
down the policy for cluster development and oversee the implementation, and strongly believes that these announcement would have definite
bearing on the growth and development of SSI sector. 
 
20.6     Working of cluster approach to the promotion and    proliferation of Small Scale Industries
           
20.6.1  The Ministry of SSI Stated that the present approach of Ministry of SSI for cluster developments is a holistic one, focusing on
interventions in various areas like technology, marketing, skill upgradation etc. selected on the basis of assessment of felt needs of the
Cluster.  The Programme is implemented with active involvement of various Cluster Actors such as Small Scale Industrial Units, Industry
Associations, Business Development Services Providers, Policy Makers etc. The process of cluster development usually consists of the  steps
as Selection of the Cluster;  Selection of a Cluster Development Agent ; Diagnostic Study ; Preparation of Action Plan for intervention ;
Approval of the project and release of funds through leveraging ; Implementation of Trust Building between Cluster Actors and Cluster
Development Agent, and also among Cluster Actors; Monitoring and Evaluation and Self  Management Phase.      The Ministry of Small
Scale Industries, through its successful collaborative efforts with UNIDO, and also independently on its own, has initiated and completed a
series of Cluster Development initiatives spread all over the country.  Till date, 81 clusters have been selected for interventions in this
manner. 
 
20.6.2  Cluster Development Programme aims at selection of suitable clusters  for development under a holistic approach.  The criteria for
selection of Clusters are based on its significance in terms of nature of products and its contribution to production, export and employment. 
Existence of critical gaps in respect of technology, quality, marketing support, common facility etc. are also taken into account. The Ministry
of Small Scale Industries has recently circulated detailed guidelines for selection and implementation of interventions to small industry
clusters under the SICDP. Cluster Development is being implemented either through the   field network of SISIs or in collaboration with
reputed  agencies like Entrepreneurship Development Institute at Ahmedabad and National Resource Centre for Cluster Development,
Hyderabad.  The results are highly encouraging in general. 
 
20.6.3  The Committee notes that under Cluster Development approach, the key problem faced by Micro Small & Medium Enterprises
(MSMEs) are being addressed. The Committee understands that the isolated Enterprises are unable to achieve economies of scales, lack
negotiating power  and have limited access to credit, strategic information, technology and market etc, therfore, such   enterprises especially
the Small & Micro ones can significantly increase their comparative advantage by mutual- cooperation and building linkages with private &
public service providers.  The Committee  views that there is the need to     build competitive strength through cost reduction, value chain
upgradation and utilization of collective economies of scale. The committee, therefore, recommends that   Cluster Development  must focus
on reducing the isolation faced by MSMEs by strengthening the linkages among all cluster stakeholders to coordinate action and pool
resources for a common development goal.

Institute (CMTI), Bangalore joined hands with NSIC and established a state of the art Metrological Laboratory in the NSIC Technical

the SSI units.
 
21.5     Comparative study of Small Scale Industries in regard to comparative Competitiveness of Indian Small Scale Industries
 
21.5.1             NSIC has not conducted such comparative studies so far. However, partner institutions abroad and SSI delegations that NSIC
organises, act as a medium to understand the comparative market situations in different countries. The principal barriers to competitiveness of
Indian Small Industries are large scale technological obsolescence, an antiquated mind set which insulates the industry from global market
trends, lack of a technology strategy, lack of structured business plans and  absence of networking between small and large industries.
 
21.5.2  The Committee feels the need for undertaking the Comparative study of Small Scale Industries in regards to comparative
Competitiveness of Indian Small Scale Industries. The Committee recommends that efforts should be made to combat the barriers to
competitiveness of Indian Small Industries viz. the large scale technological obsolescence, an antiquated mind set which insulates the industry
from global market trends, lack of a technology strategy, lack of structured business plans and absence of networking between small and large

22.9     Working of Central Institute of Tools Design 
 
22.9.1  The Central Institute of Tool Design (CITD) was established at Hyderabad in 1968 by the Government of India with the assistance of
UNDP & ILO. It was the first of its kind in the country established by the Government of India. The aim was to fulfil the tooling needs of the
Small scale Industries in the field of Tool Design & Manufacture and training of technical personnel in these fields.
 
22.9.2  The Institute promotes growth of small scale industries by facilitating development and production of tools, moulds, dies etc. and
making available trained manpower and technical consultancy services to SSI sector etc.  The Institute also assists industry in upgrading their
technology and developing the skill of their employees, through various vocational training programmes.
 
22.9.3  The CITD has trained around 10000 persons in various skill up-gradation courses like CAD/CAM, CNC Technology etc. during the
last five years. In addition, around 1300 units have been provided tooling services both for production and design. The support to SSIs is
being further enhanced by regularly upgrading the facilities and services of the Institute, by way of introducing state-of-the-art machinery &
training facilities needed by the industry, etc. The CITD Hyderabad, is, however, planning to set up an extension centre at Chennai in view of
the needs of the SMEs in and around Chennai.
 
22.9.4  The Committee desires for  opening more branches of Central Institute of Tool Design to  facilitate the services all over the country 
for  providing services to SMEs in their respective regions.

31.0     Comparative study to assess the Export potential of SSI Sector
 
31.1     M/s. A.C. Nielsen on behalf of Ministry of SSI has done an evaluation study.   As per the findings and recommendations of the said
study, the major export markets identified having potential to enhance SSIs exports (including these States) are US, EU and Japan.  The
potential items of SSIs have been categorized  into three broad category such as :-
 
Potential items of SSI amongst the top 100 imports of the major markets not figuring in top 100 exports of India to the major markets:-  The
product groups that hold potential for SSI exports are agriculture, marine and allied products alongwith engineering/ electrical/ electronic
product group.  Japan is a potential market for exporting agriculture, marine and allied products whereas the European union and the US can
be tapped for enhancing SSI exports of engineering/electrical and electronic items.
Potential items of SSI amongst the top 100 exports of India to the major markets not figuring in top 100 imports of the major markets :-  The
major thrust areas for SSI exports are agriculture and allied, chemicals, plastic items, leather and textile product groups, The US and EU have
been identified as the potential markets for textile whereas export of chemicals product groups holds a potential for Japan.
Potential items of SSI amongst the top 100 imports of the major markets and also figuring in top 100 exports of India to the major markets:

items.  The EU has been identified as the potential market for textiles including sports equipments whereas export of leather items holds

31.2     Another interesting feature to note is the consistent increase in the %age share of SSI exports in the field of electronics and computer
software.  The %age share has more than doubled from 5.40% in the year 1999-2000 to 13.12% in 2001-2002. As regards the steps
undertaken to increase the export potential of SSI sector, this Ministry has been participating in product specific as well as general exhibitions
in India and abroad every year, and has been organizing export marketing training programmes and also on packaging for exports.  Sector
Specific Market Studies are conducted for selected SSI categories.  Individual assistance for participation in overseas fairs, study tours and
also production of publicity materials for overseas publicity are provided to the SSI entrepreneurs.  
 
31.3     The Committee desires that the Government should take benefits of the Comparative study undertaken by M/s. A.C. Nielsen to assess
the Export potential of SSI Sector and  increase the export potential of SSI sector .  The Committee desires that the Ministry of SSI may 
apprise the committee of the  outcome of the strategy for increasing the export potential of SSI sector as per the findings of the study
undertaken.
 
32.0     Process modification and product diversification in SMEs
 
32.1     Six Process and Product Development Centres were set up in mid eighties with the assistance of UNIDO / UNDP.  These Centres
cater to the need of technology upgradation for small scale sector including process modification and product diversification in different
product groups, viz., Glass & Ceramics, Foundry & Forging, Essential oils, Sports goods, Hand Tools, Electronics items. SIDO has also set
up nine Tool Rooms which are providing product development services. These are also providing trained manpower to industry for
improvement of product and processes. These are being upgraded from time to time to meet the present day need.
32.2     Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology Upgradation in Small Scale Industries has been started by this office in year
2000 which provides 15% subsidy to selected sub sectors on institutional finance for technology upgradation.  The technology related needs
for process modification and product diversification can be fulfilled by SSI sector through the scheme.  Action is being taken to enhance the
scope of this scheme to cover more areas by O/o DC(SSI).
 
32.3     The Committee is of the considered view that there is always the  need for technology upgradation, product  and  process development
in Small Scale sector, therefore, the  Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology Upgradation undertaken by  Office of  DC(SSI)

33.0     The Chinese challenge              
 
33.1     The export-import data obtained from Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry   indicate that India’s imports
from China have increased to some extent from Rs.5559 crore during 1999-2000 to Rs.30413 crore during 2004-2005.   However, exports of
India to China have grown significantly from Rs.2336 crore (1999-2000) to Rs.24015 crore during 2004-05 .             To facilitate cost
reduction, design, process-modification and product diversification to make the Indian SSI products more competitive, the Ministry of SSI has
modernized its  PPDCs and  Tool Rooms to meet this challenge. In addition, the field offices of SIDO i.e Small Industries Service Institutes
(SISIs) have set up Technology Resource Centers (TRCs) to advise and enable the SSIs to upgrade themselves to compete in the global
market.
 
33.2     Moreover, a Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for investment in technology upgradation provides subsidy and credit for
technology upgradation.  Sector-specific programmes for modernization of stone, toy industry, lock industry and machine tools are also in
operation. Limit under Excise Exemption scheme has been enhanced from Rs.50 lakh to Rs.1 crore.  Scheme   for providing financial
assistance to SSI Associations for setting up testing laboratories.  Scheme providing for assistance to SSI units in obtaining ISO 9000 & ISO
14001 certification.  Investment ceiling in handmade tools, hosiery, stationery, drugs & pharmaceuticals and   sport shoes has been increased
from Rs.1 crore to Rs.5 crores to enable the units to go in for technology upgradation and modernization.  The SSI sector is being prepared
and made aware of various provisions of WTO, anti-dumping, Intellectual Property Rights, Geographical Indications, etc. through seminars,
workshops, etc. Workshops/trainings have been initiated on procedure for obtaining bar coding.  A scheme providing for 75   per cent  of the
total expenses incurred by SSI units in bar coding registration has been launched.
 
33.3     The Committee observes that our market is fluxed with Chinese products manufactured in Small Scale segment, therefore, there is
urgent need for taking corrective  steps for  cost reduction, design, process-modification and production diversification to make the India SSI
product more competitive to combat the Chinese challenge.
 
34.0     Credit  linked Capital Subsidy Scheme
 
34.1     The Ministry of Small Scale Industries (SSI) is operating a scheme for technology upgradation of Small Scale Industries (SSI) called
the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS). The Scheme aims at facilitating technology upgradation by providing  upfront capital
subsidy to  SSI units, including tiny, khadi, village and coir industrial units, on institutional finance (credit) availed of by them for
modernisation of their production equipment (plant and machinery) and techniques.  The Scheme (pre-revised) provided for 12 per cent 
capital subsidy to SSI units, including  tiny units, on institutional finance availed of by them for induction of well established and improved
technology in selected sub-sectors/products approved under the Scheme. The eligible amount of subsidy calculated under the pre-revised 
scheme was based on the actual loan amount not exceeding Rs.40 lakh. 
 
34.2     Due to insufficient investment and lack of awareness of both the quality standards and access to modern technologies, a large
percentage of SSI units continue with outdated technology and plant & machinery.  With increasing competition due to liberalisation of the
economy, the survival and growth of the SSI units are critically dependent on their modernisation and technological upgradation. 
Upgradation of both the process of manufacture and corresponding plant and machinery is necessary for the small enterprises  to reduce the
cost of production and remain price competitive at a time when cheaper products are easily available in the global market. 
 
34.3     It is in this background that the Finance Minister made an announcement in the Budget Speech of 2004-05 to raise the ceiling for loans
under the Scheme from Rs. 40 lakh to Rs. 1 crore and rate of subsidy from 12 per cent to 15 per cent.  Further, in the light of the experience
gathered in implementing the Scheme,  certain other modifications were also required  to make it  more useful to  the  SSI  units, including
tiny, khadi, village and coir industrial  units,  in taking up technology upgradation on a larger scale. After considering these issues, the CLCSS
has been amended with effect from September 29, 2005 and the ceiling on loans under the Scheme has been raised  from Rs. 40 lakh to Rs. 1
crore and the  rate of subsidy has been enhanced from 12 per cent to 15 per cent;
 
34.4     The target group for the scheme are SSI units, including tiny, khadi, village and coir industrial units (falling under the purview of the
Ministry of ARI). The scope of the scheme has been widened to include tiny,  khadi, village and coir industrial units (falling under the
purview of the Ministry of ARI) to cover khadi and village industrial units and coir industrial units.  The basis for the selection of the target
group is that the scheme has primarily been conceived for providing subsidy to the small and tiny enterprises in India. However, industry 
graduating from small scale to medium scale on account to sanction of additional loan under CLCSS are also eligible for assistance under the
scheme. 
 
34.5     Presently, the scheme is in operation up to March 31, 2007 or till the time sanction of aggregate capital subsidy disbursed by the nodal
agencies/banks reaches Rs.600 crore, whichever is earlier.   The amount of subsidy sanctioned between 2001-02 and 2005-06 is Rs.36.65
crore (approx.).  However, most of it ( Rs. 18.14 crore approx.) has been sanctioned during 2005-06. This shows that the amendments made in
the existing CLCSS guidelines has enabled more and more   tiny and small scale  industrial units to undertake modernisation through availing
of  capital subsidy under the CLCSS.

34.5.4  Consequent upon the increase of ceiling of loan from Rs. 40 lakh to  Rs 1.0 crore and increase in rate of subsidy from 12 per cent to 15
per cent from September 29, 2005, the progress under the CLCSS has been encouraging. While the amount of subsidy sanctioned between
2001-02 and 2005-06 is Rs.36.65 crore (approx.),  most of it ( Rs. 18.14 crore approx.) has been sanctioned during 2005-06. During 2005-06,
only 200 units were assisted upto November, 2005 by providing capital subsidy of Rs.5.53 crore (approximately),  whereas,  between
December 2005 and March 2006,  501 units availed Rs. 12.61 crore (approx.) capital subsidy under this scheme. This shows that the
amendments made in the existing CLCSS guidelines have encouraged  more and more   tiny and small scale  industrial units to undertake

800 units.   During 2006-07, it is expected that   1200 units will be covered under the CLCSS. 
 
34.5.5  Some of sub-sectors/products which have been  included, in addition to existing sub-sectors/products, for assistance under the CLCSS

Graphite and Phosphate , Khadi and Village Industries, Coir and Coir Products, Steel Re-rolling and /or Pencil Ingot making Industries ,Zinc
Sulphate ,Welding Electrodes , Sewing Machine Industry . The budget provision in the year 2006-07 for the CLCSS is likely to be sufficient
in view of the widened base of the scheme. However, depending on the progress of the scheme, steps will be taken to re-appropriate
additional funds for meeting the requirements of the CLCSS. 
 
34.5.6  The Committee takes note that SIDO faces  some problems in implementation of Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme(CLCSS) 
which interalia include  lack of awareness about the scheme on the part of beneficiary units, lack of awareness about the scheme among the

awareness level of industry associations, Banks and other concerned agencies , take up regular review of progress of the scheme in the

34.6 Standard/ quality of technology
 
34.6.1  The value of SSI exports from India has been growing consistently and SSI contributes as   much as 34% to the nation’s exports.  Thus
the Indian SSI products are competitive in the global market for quite a number of products.  In order to further improve the  competitive
advantage for domestic products in the international market various  steps have been initiated viz Assisting Industry Associations to establish
Product Testing Centres under  SIDO’s Scheme of financial support for the same ; Financial assistance to units to obtain ISO : 9000 and ISO :
14001 Certification and Registration for Bar Coding ; Opening Mini Tool Rooms under the SIDO Scheme of financial support to the State
Governments for the same ; Scheme for National Awards for Quality Products, R&D etc and Various Schemes for marketing support and
export being implemented by SIDO and NSIC.
 
34.6.2  The Committee desires that the Standard/ quality of technology employed in domestic Small Scale Industries must be  comparable
enough to technology employed by SMEs in  other developing/developed countries so as to imbibe competitiveness in domestic SSI products
vis-a-vis foreign products in view of its influx as the consequent of removal of quantitative restrictions in the wake of WTO guidelines. The
Committee feels that  WTO guidelines awareness programme and  techonological imorovement schemes together can imbibe competitiveness
in domestic SSI products vis-a-vis foreign products.

36.0     Problems being faced by SIDO in the implementation of programmes encouraging SMEs
           
36.1     The Committee has been  apprised that SIDO is implementing several schemes/programmes for the promotion and development of the
SSI sector in the country.  Most of these schemes/programmes are aimed at augmenting the credit flow to the SSI sector and are linked with
the banks/financial institutions.  The banks are, however, not favourably inclined to finance the SSI sector for various reasons like adverse
risk perception,  lack of credit rating facilities, higher transaction cost in processing of large number of loan applications, etc.  Moreover,
some of the schemes are optional for the banks to participate in their implementation. Furthermore, the implementation of the schemes/
programmes is also dependent on the willingness of the beneficiaries (i.e. the SSI units/ entrepreneurs) and the State Governments. The State
Governments have a major role to play in the implementation of some of the schemes/ programmes by way of providing matching financial
contribution, infrastructural facilities, fiscal incentives/ concessions etc.            The Ministry of SSI has  launched  a scheme on credit rating,
which includes providing financial assistance to the SSI units for obtaining credit rating. The Ministry of SSI has taken up the matter with all
the Public Sector Banks for dissemination of information on schemes/programmes at the branch level and among the SSI entrepreneurs. The
SSI Associations have also been asked to play a pro-active role in increasing awareness about the schemes/ programmes/ facilities being
implemented for the SSI sector among the SSI entrepreneurs.
 
36.2     The Committee is of the view that working of SIDO  must be strengthened so much so that it can encourage emerging SMEs to catch
up the global trend . There is a need to encourage SSI units for obtaining credit rating and setting up of exclusive credit rating agencies for the
SSI sector. There is further need for wider and effective dissemination of information on the schemes/ facilities being provided by the banks
to the SSI sector at the branch level and among the entrepreneurs.  In addition, the State Governments need to provide an enabling
environment for development and promotion of the SSI sector through provision of fiscal concessions/incentives to the sector, better
infrastructure facilities etc. for facilitating smooth implementation of the schemes of SIDO. The Committee is of the considered view that the 
Small and Medium Enterprises Development Bill, 2005, would  strengthen SIDDO.  Besides, SIDO may be entrusted with the effective  role
in the  implemetaion of  promotional package for the Small scale sector which  is under formulation.
 
37.0     Working of Small Industries Development Organization (SIDO )
 
37.1     Keeping in view the fast changing scenario, SIDO, which is an apex body in the Ministry of Small Scale Industries to formulate
policies and programmes for SSI Sector, has taken lead in computerized information networking  so as to be able to be the main information
provider in the Country and has consequently launched its independent web site with a net work of 30 locations in the field.  Accordingly
there is change in the role of its field institutions, which apart from providing general assistance by way of techno-economic counseling and
consultancy, conducting of surveys, providing project profiles, are stressing more on training and dissemination of information in different
fields which include information on availability of new technology, existing Central/State statutory and non-statutory requirements, existing
policies and programmes and the source of assistance etc. 
 
37.2     The Committee appreciates the working of Small Industries Development Organization (SIDO) as an apex body in the Ministry of
Small Scale Industries so far as the  formulateion of the policies and programmes for SSI Sector is concerned , however,  role  of SIDO can be
strengthened in the promotion and development of SMEs by  emphasizing  on sensitization programmes, which include sensitization
programmes on WTO, Intellectual Proprietary Rights (IPR), information and encouragement sunrise industries, cluster development and
modernization and technical up-gradation. 
 
37.3     The Committee hopes that SIDO would play the prominant role  in the  promotion of small scale industries through various
promotional programmes and services provided by its field offices e.g. SISIs, RTCs, FTSs, Autonomous including PPDCs/Tool Rooms &
Branch  SISIs and thus prove milestone in converting the SEs into MEs.

39.1     The Objective of the Credit Guarantee Scheme to ensure better flow of credit to small and tiny enterprises by minimizing the risk
perception of financial institutions. This will give greater comfort level to banks and also help financing without collateral security. The
mechanism of the scheme is by setting up a corpus fund with contribution from the Government of India and the Small Industries
Development Bank of India (SIDBI) in the ratio of 4:1.   At present, the size of the corpus fund is Rs. 1181.55 crore.  As the Operating
Agency  a trust has been  set up by SIDBI/GOI and serviced by SIDBI. CMD, SIDBI is the Chairman of the Trust; AS & DC (SSI) is the
Vice-Chairman of the Trust; two other members are Chairman, Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the
Trust. The lending institutions can have loans guaranteed by payment of one-time guarantee fee of 2.5 per cent and an annual service fee of
0.75 per cent of the credit sanctioned to the Trust, the implementing agency. The Eligible Institutions  
 are Commercial Banks – public and
private, select regional rural banks (RRBs), North East Development Finance Corporation (NEDFi), National Small Industries Corporation
(NSIC) and SIDBI. So far the Claim Settlement is concerned ,  after 2-year lock-in period; settlement up to 75 per cent pending recovery
proceedings, balance 25 percent on completion of recovery proceedings.  The Extent of Guaranteeis75% of loans up to Rs.25 lakh. The
Maximum Risk cover is  75% of the risk cover subject to a ceiling of Rs.18.75 lakh.  Interest rate payable by borrower not to exceed 3%
beyond  PLR of lender.  The Scheme was announced on 30August 2000 and became operational in January 2001.
 
39.2     The scheme was launched with a view to alleviate the problems of collateral security faced by the small enterprises, particularly first
generation entrepreneurs, and to remove the impediments in flow of credit to Small enterprises sector. The problems in the implementation of
the scheme pertains to low level of awareness about the scheme amongst the field level officers of MLIs, negative mindset of the MLIs due to
greater volume of administrative work in the small enterprises lending and may be their bad experience in the past on a similar scheme,
bankers’ traditional/usual comfort with collateral security and perceived high risk nature of small enterprises sector. These problems of the
bank branches need to be seriously addressed by the management of the banks.  By enhancing the awareness about the scheme among the
field level officers of MLIs through seminars/training, the progress under the scheme could be improved. Furthermore, enhancement of the

39.12   Collateral/third party guarantee
 
39.12.1            CGTSI has been making concerted efforts to create awareness about the credit guarantee scheme among the branch managers
of banks by organizing Regional / Zonal based workshops-cum-training programmes where the information relating to the guarantee scheme
and the benefits available are explained in detail.  Besides, CGTSI has been attending the State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC) meetings
and other meetings convened by RBI, GoI, Industry Associations and other stakeholders and providing the information relating to the scheme
for the benefit of the participants.  In order to change the mindset of the Branch Managers, the awareness programmes have to continue for
some more time.  However, the coverage of 12727 cases during the financial year 2005-06 reflects the increasing acceptance of the Scheme
by Banks.
 
39.12.2            The Committee observes that despite the provision of the loans (up to 25.00 lakh) without collateral/third party guarantee and
the guidelines  of the Reserve Bank of India thereto, Banks insist  on the collateral security and the third party guarantee and despite the
committee's repeated recommendation to change the mind set of the Branch Managers, nothing fruitful has come out, therefore, the
Committee desires that Government should come out with  the suitable and sustainable measures for effective working of the scheme as per
its declared vision and mission.

39.14.3            The Committee wanted to know as to why the Plan Outlay was  drastically  reduced to the tune of Rs.106.00 crore in BE 2006-
07 in comparison to Rs.180.00 during the year 2005-06 and   the target set for year 2005-06 and 2006-07 . The committee was apprised that

expected to be lodged by the MLIs. The Hon’ble Finance Minister, Govt. of India, has proposed a budget outlay of Rs. 118 crore for the FY

functioning of units, which are covered under Credit Guarantee Scheme.  Since the guarantee cover is to the extent of 75% of the loan, the

CGTSI obtains periodic data from the MLIs regarding the status of the accounts covered under the scheme.  Moreover, CGTSI can conduct
inspection of accounts covered under the scheme, on sample basis. 
 
39.14.5            The Member banks / lending institutions (MLIs) have been suggesting increase in the credit amount for coverage under the
credit guarantee scheme.  As per the present guidelines, the loans upto Rs.25 lakh extended by the MLIs to the eligible borrowers are provided
guarantee cover under the Credit Guarantee Scheme.  Since the investment limit in plant and machinery in respect of small scale industrial
units is Rs.1 crore and in select sectors upto Rs.5 crore, the loan limit for coverage under the scheme could be suitably increased.  Other need-
based modifications in the procedural aspects of the Scheme have been carried out by CGTSI from time to time.
 
39.14.6            The Committee notes the  announcement made  by   the Finance Minister  in is Budget Speech (2006-07) on the success of
Credit Guarantee Scheme and the consequent   promotion and proliferation of SMEs :-
 
(a)        Raising  the corpus of the Credit Guarantee Fund from Rs. 1.132 crore at end-March 2006 to Rs. 2,500 crore in five years.  In 2006-
07,  proposing  to provide a sum of Rs. 118 crore;
 
(b)        Advising  Credit Guarantee Trust for Small Industries (CGTSI) to  reduce the one time guarantee fee from 2.5 per cent to 1.5 per cent
for all loans; and
 
(c)        Extending  insurance cover to approximately 30,000 borrowers, identified as chief promoters, under the CGTSI.  The sum assured
would be Rs. 200,000 per beneficiary and the premium will be paid by CGTSI.
 
39.14.7            The Committee is in agreement with the   Credit Guarantee Fund  to be increased to Rs.2500 crore over the next 5 years with
total contribution from GOI of Rs.2000 crore and Rs.500 crore from SIDBI respectively, therefore, approves the provision for the  sum of Rs.
118 crore during the year 2006-07.  the committee is quite convinced that   higher the corpus fund, the credibility of CGTSI would get
enhanced in the opinion  of the lending institutions seeking guarantee cover so that in case of default by SSI borrowers, CGTSI would be in a
position to meet claims raised against the guarantees issued by it, therefore, the committee, believes that  the corpus fund would be  helpful 
in  meeting  the likely contingent liabilities arising out of the guarantees issued by CGTSI.

41.23   National Commission on Enterprises  in the unorganized/informal sectors
41.23.  The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS) has been constituted to examine the problems
confronting the enterprise in the unorganised/informal sector and make appropriate recommendations to provide technical, marketing and
credit support to these enterprises. The NCEUS is proposing the formation of Growth Poles in different parts of the country with a view to
integrating within a geographical location a number of clusters of production units engaged in manufacturing services and non-farm activities
and facilitating the expansion of production and employment in small and micro enterprises. The Growth Poles would incorporate the concept
of the Scheme of Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas (PURA) that has been advocated by Dr. A.P.J. Abdual Kalam, President of
India.
           
41.23.2            In the first instance, the Commission is proposing a few pilot Growth Poles for consideration by the Government as mentioned
in the Finance Minister’s Budget Speech, 2005-06. For the conduct of the proposed pilots, a number of multi-product
industrial/artisanal/handloom and handicrafts clusters that have the potential to evolve into Growth Pole are being identified. The NCEUS
proposes to delineate Growth Poles in the NER and Sikkim Region to give a fillip to the unorganized sector enterprises in this region. The
Plan outlay of Rs 3.30 crore in be 2006-07 is proposed to be utilized for conducting detailed technical and feasibility studies and preparation
of Detailed project reports for Growth Poles in the region and commence the projects in the region.
           
41.23.3            The idea of Growth Poles is an extension of the idea of clusters based on the economics of inter-dependence of different
producing units in a particular geographical concentration, creating the scope for duplication and extension of those activities in larger
contiguous areas that would eventually cover the whole of the country. These Growth Poles would also combine effectively the essential
features of the proposed scheme of PURA of providing urban amenities in rural areas. The inter-dependence of these units allows them to
enjoy external economies from their simultaneous and complementary functioning. Such positive externalities are derived from (a) forward
and backward linkages in productive activities, such as units using each other’s demands for inputs and production of output, both within and
outside the area; (b) use of common facilities for social overhead capital like road, other forms of transport, communications and marketing
connections, both within the country and for exports; (c) utilizing common services of education, health, sanitation, housing, water etc.;  (d)
allowing inter-linkages of different services to develop a network with the clusters of activities.  The main idea is that if the units were to
function in isolation from each other, the costs of these units would be much higher than when they are acting together.  If nothing else, the
fixed costs are spread over a broader base.  Indeed, the issue is not only one of exploiting positive externalities; it also becomes more cost
effective to cope with negative externalities, like generation of waste and other forms of pollution. The Commission is of the view that by
addressing the problems of the industrial clusters as a group, these clusters can take advantage of on-going programmes and bring about a
convergence and synergy through the Growth Poles. This would benefit the unorganized/ informal sector as this sector would be thus in a
position to take advantage of the generation of these externalities.

41.24.1            The Committee finds that  the enterprises based in the NER and Sikkim are predominantly handlooms and handicraft based

Committee feels that the complementarities that are proposed to be built up as a result of intervention in the Growth Pole would  benefit the
unorganized/ informal sector as a result of forward and backward linkages in productive activities  .

43.0     Tiny and Micro Enterprises
 
43.1     Tiny enterprises are such units which have investment in plant and machinery upto Rs.25 lakh. As such all such industrial activities
which are eligible for registration as SSI are also eligible for registration in the tiny sector as long as its investment in plant and machinery is
up to the prescribed limit of Rs.25 lakh. The activities in khadi and coir industry predominantly in rural areas and have investment below Rs.
25 lakh and hence are covered under tiny/micro enterprises in agro & rural industries sector.
 
43.2     A provision has been made in the General Budget (2006-07) in regard to the promotion of Tiny and Micro Enterprises.  A provision of
Rs. 324.98 crore has been made for PMRY under the Ministry of ARI in the Budget 2006-2007.  For Micro Finance Programme, a provision
of Rs. 32.28 crore (including provision for NER & Sikkim) has been made in the Budget 2006-2007 under the Ministry of SSI.
 
43.3   The Committee is of the view that concrete  steps may be taken to strengthen and streamline the tiny sector and in order to give tiny
sector an organized outlook. The Committee finds that Small Scale Industries (SSIs) including tiny units in the country  have enough
competitive strength to withstand the impact of free imports and intense global competition.  Government should launch awareness
programme  of the WTO provision and international  environment for preparing the small scale sector including tiny sector to meet the
challenges of globalization. Government should  constantly monitor  the impact of the removal of QRs and WTO Agreements on the economy
including the SSIs in the country. The committee is aware that the removal of QRs have exposed the SSIs to a greater competition, yet the SSI
sector including tiny sector  is bound to grow.  
 
44.0     Mechanism of institutional arrangement
 
44.1     Almost all over the world, the policies are devised to meet the requirement of  Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Sector. In
Sweden, France , Germany, Belgium, Portugal, Switzerland, China and many other developed and developing countries their exist SME 
oriented policies .
 
44.2     In the context of globalisation there is a growing feeling in certain quarters that India should also adopt the SME Concept. S.P Gupta
Committee while aiming at three-tier definition on Tiny, Small and Medium Enterprises in its study report on development of Small Scale
Sector, has also shown preference for the concept of SMEs. On 9
th January 2004 the then Finance Minister announced a fund of Rs.10, 000
crores for SME Sector.  The Finance Minister while presenting the budget for 2004-05, has said that there is need to provide some space for
SSIs to grow into medium enterprises. From the above, it emerges that the issue of SME Sector has come into consideration but a final view
has yet to be taken on this issue.
 
44.3     The Finance Minister in his Budget speech (2005-06) has reiterated ,” In recent years , our approach to small scale industry has
evolved , and now we are inclined to treat the sector as the small and medium enterprises sector”
 
44.4     While SSIs have been defined in India , definition of Medium sector has yet to come. Certainly the upper limit of the defined
investment limit of the SSI sector will be the demarcation line delineating the SSI from Medium sector. The mechanism of institutional
arrangement, modalities of working and incentives in respect of SSI is already existing.  As far as that of Medium sector is concerned it would
be worked out as soon as a policy decision on Medium sector is taken. It is worth while to mention that after recognizing the importance of
SME concept, Office of the DC (SSI) is in the process of formulation of a “ Small and Medium Enterprises Development Bill , 2005” which
inter-alia, incorporates measures of promotion of Medium Enterprises .
 
44.5     The Committee is in agreement with  the the Finance Minister who has recognized  the  small scale industries as the engine of 
growth.  The committee is also of the view that  finance  to SSI must be treated as financing to  SME in order to give the SSI units to grow
into Medium Enterprises, therefore, recommends that concerted efforts step must be undertaken to meet the requirement of Small and
Medium Enterprises (SME). Adequate steps must be taken to promote and proliferate the  Medium Enterprises. And due incentive and

Institutional support in rehabilitation of Sick SSI units
 
45.1     Replying to the Committee’s query as how to utilize the institutional support in rehabilitation of Sick SSI units and promotion of SSI
Sectors, the Ministry of SSI stated that  the State Level Inter-Institutional Committee (SLIIC) has been set up in each State under the

with the problems of co-ordination for rehabilitation of sick SSI units at the State level. The meetings of SLIIC are generally held at quarterly
intervals.  A Sub-Committee of SLIIC has also been set up under the convenorship of SLBC convenor bank (depending on the number of
individual rehabilitation cases to be discussed) wherein borrowers and bankers concerned are invited to discuss the issue on one-to-one basis.
           
45.2     The Committee is however, of the view that all for effective  rehabilitation of Sick SSI units and promotion of SSI Sectors  all the
Regional Offices of RBI should ensure that meetings of State Level Inter-Institutional Committee SLIICs are convened at regular periodical
intervals and the meetings are attended by the senior officials of banks/financial institutions so as to serve the desired objective. The
representatives of the local SSI Associations should also be invited to the meetings of SLIIC, which should play a major role in rehabilitation
of sick units. SLIICs should address the  issues regarding delay in carrying out viability studies and initiating nursing programmes of viable
units as also progress in revival of units, which have been placed under the nursing programme. Further, the issues relating to the progress

speedy rehabilitation of sick SSI units identified as potentially viable.
 46.0    Sunrise industries in the SMEs sector
 
46.1     The office of DC(SSI) has conducted various information/training programmes in respect of sunrise industries in the SSI sector. These
programmes have been conducted in areas like IPRs, IT & Bio-Technology.   Various Entrepreneurial Development Programmes on Bio
Technology are being conducted in SIDO’s field offices. Technical officers of SIDO have recently been deputed for training Programme
organized by SIDO in collaboration with Bio Technology Consortium of India so as to engage them in Bio Technology Training programme. 
Nano technology being a new and relatively capital intensive as well as R&D intensive activity, is yet to be focused in the SSI sector.
           
46.2     The promotion of IT will go a long way in encouraging sunrise industries as most of the sunrise industries have a strong IT component
built into them.  Training for IT and IT enabled services has been taken up in a big way in the SISIs.   IPR protection and management of
rapid up-scaling through infusion of technology is important for development of SSI sector in these areas.  The Office of DCSSI has been
conducting IPR training programmes all over the country for the last few years.. Enablement of the entrepreneurs to take up the issue of IPR
protection and management of rapid up-scaling of operation on priority basis is expected through these programmes.  The small scale
entrepreneurs are being sensitized towards the need for protection and methodology to be adopted for IPR management through not only
diffusion and upgradation of technology but also employing existing IPR resources for the purpose.
           
46.3     For the development of Biotechnology related industry in SSI sector, a Biotechnology Cell was created in the office of DC(SSI) on
16.08.2002. The main aim of this cell is to promote awareness amongst the SSI entrepreneurs on the  benefits of Biotechnology and to
disseminate techno-economic information on various feasible biotech products in the  SSI sector. To  further strengthen our field offices for
the promotion of Biotechnology in the SSI sector, a group of 28 officers from SISIs including the office of  DC(SSI)  were imparted advance
training   during 11
th to 13th January, 2006   by  the Biotech Consortium India Limited (BCIL) at Chandigarh.   During the year 2005-06,  12 
one-day sensitization programmes on Biotechnoloy were  held  by different SISI in close coordination with the  BCIL and  the Department of
Biotechnology, Govt. of India.  A set of  Project Profiles on  commercially viable  Bio-tech products in the SSI sector has been brought out
for the guidance of the  prospective   entrepreneurs.
           
46.4     IPR protection and management of rapid up-scaling through infusion of technology is important for the development of small
enterprises in these areas. To generate awareness amongst SSI on IPR related issues,  various one-day sensitisation programmes are being
organised since 2001-02.  During the year 2005-06, 14 such programmes have been conducted    by SISIs all over the country. A group of 28
SIDO officers have been trained on IPR during 25-26
th May 2005 under the guidance of Dr. P.Ganguli, visiting Professor, IIT, Mumbai and
Chairman – Vision IPR.  With the initiatives of the office of   DC (SSI), Kulu Shawls has been registered under the Geographical Indication
(GI) Act and efforts are being made to assist a group of Industries at Bikaner and Coimbatore to register Bikaneri Bhujia and Wet Grinder
respectively under the GI Act.                                                                  
 
46.5     Under the “ Promotional Package for the SSI Sector”, the office of DC(SSI)  in the Ministry of SSI has proposed to launch a
“Financial Assistance Scheme” for registered small scale / tiny units for adoption of patent in India and abroad.  The scheme envisages to tap
the vast innovative potential of the small scale entrepreneurs, enabling them to become technology-based entrepreneurs.  The objective of the

 47.0    Working of SME Development Fund
47.1     Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has set up “SME Growth Fund” (SGF), a national level venture capital fund
focused at the SME sector.  This is a unique initiative sponsored by SIDBI jointly with major public sector banks such as State Bank of India,
Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda and several other major nationalized banks.  The life of fund is 8 years. SGF was formally launched in
October 2004.  It has started the operations by making investment commitments and has sanctioned investment in two companies.  It expects
to commit major portion in next 3 to 4 years.  The fund is being managed by SIDBI venture Capital Ltd. (SVCL), a wholly owned subsidiary
of SIDBI. SVCL has an extensive expertise in early stage venture investments and familiarization with local as well as international practices
in venture capital industry.  It is already managing a fund of Rs.100 crore for the IT/ITES sectors viz, National Venture Fund for Software and
IT Industry (NFSIT).  The skills and experience of the investment team, the emphasis on value creation and its linkages place SVCL in a
unique position to partner with an enterprise in its growth. SGF has been established with an objective to meet the long term risk capital of
SME units, to enable them to achieve rapid growth rates and maintain their competitive edge in domestic and international markets.  SGF is a
general fund and shall make primarily equity/equity-related capital investments in accordance with SEBI guidelines in units operating in
various sectors such as life sciences, biotechnology, retailing, pharmaceuticals, light engineering and information technology.  These projects
should be backed by a management team with proven track record and should have a sustainable competitive intellectual property, technology
or a well differentiated market positioning with potential of achieving and sustaining a leading market position.  
47.2     The Committee understands that SME Development Fund promoted by SIDBI/banks with a corpus of Rs.500 crore aims at  funding 
export oriented and high technology SME. The Committee advises the Ministry of SSI to examine whether   there is the need to enhance the
said corpus fund to proliferate the SMEs, and if yes,  the strategy/ mechanism to support SMEs in knowledge-  based industries such as
Pharma, Bio-tech. and I.T. to this fund. The Committee would like to know the progress made in this regard during 2005-06 and the  steps
which may further be taken during the year 2006-07 contributing to  the accredited cluster which  can play catalytic role in the advancement
of SME sector.

49.0     Towards Technology upgradation
 
49.1     To make the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) for Technology Upgradation more attractive, the amendments which 
have been made with effect from 29 September 2005 as  (a) the ceiling on loans has been raised from Rs.40 lakh to Rs.1 crore; (b) the rate of
